## Upgrading to 5.3

### Changes that do not announce themselves

- **`vector_reduce_to_style` and `versatiles reduce` count only the style
  layers of one tileset.** They used to count every style layer that names a
  source-layer, whichever source it draws from. A style drawing a basemap and
  an overlay then reduced the tileset to both, and a style drawing only another
  tileset's source reduced it to nothing, silently. Now:
  - a style drawing one vector tileset works as before. Style sources with the
    same `url` or `tiles` count as one tileset, so a style that reads it twice,
    say once for the map and once for its labels, needs nothing more;
  - a style drawing several is refused until the new `source` argument
    (`--source` for `versatiles reduce`) names the one the tileset is. The
    message lists the tilesets, and names the one whose layers the tileset has
    when only one does;
  - a style drawing none of the tileset's layers is refused.
- **Hidden style layers count for nothing.** A layer with
  `"visibility": "none"` used to keep its source-layer, features and
  properties. A map that shows such a layer at runtime needs a style with it
  visible for the reduction.
- **Properties are kept only at the zooms they are read at.** A property read
  only by a style layer drawn from z12 is stripped from the tiles below z12.
  The TileJSON still lists it. On Berlin with the VersaTiles styles this saves
  little, since nearly all of the size is in the deepest zoom.

### Pipelines

- `vector_reduce_to_style` has a new argument `source`: the IDs of the style
  sources to reduce to, one or a list. Naming one source of a tileset selects
  every source with the same URL.
- `vector_reduce_to_style` no longer drops what a style draws in these cases:
  - a legacy filter on the geometry type or feature ID (`$type`, `$id`) used
    to empty the whole layer;
  - a modern `in` that tests a substring
    (`["in", ["get", "name"], "Berlin Hbf"]`) kept only an exact match;
  - properties read by a computed name (`["get", ["concat", …]]`), through
    `["properties"]`, by a legacy `{"property": …}` function, inside `format`
    options, or as the source's `promoteId` were stripped;
  - a style source whose `maxzoom` is below the tileset's: a layer drawn above
    it was kept only in tiles MapLibre never loads.
  - a `ref` layer, which takes its source-layer, filter, zooms and layout from
    another layer, was skipped, so properties only its `paint` reads were
    stripped.
- `vector_reduce_to_style` accepts fractional layer zooms (`"minzoom": 12.5`),
  which the style spec allows and the build used to refuse.

### Command line

- `versatiles reduce` has a new option `--source`, passed on as the
  operation's `source`. It can be repeated.

### Rust library

- `versatiles_pipeline::reduce`:
  - `from_style` takes the style source IDs to reduce to (`&[String]`) and the
    tileset's layer names;
  - `LayerRequirement::properties` is a `Properties` enum: `All`, or
    `Listed` with the tile zooms each property is read at;
  - `operations` and `property_regex` are removed. `vector_reduce_to_style`
    strips properties per zoom, which `vector_filter_properties` cannot
    express, so they no longer described what runs.
